newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to deregulate sale of consigned oil - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan to deregulate sale of consigned oil - report.

text.p: As part of the opening of its oil industry, Japan will drop all restrictions on the domestic sale of oil products that are part of consignments from foreign companies, a Japanese economic newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the change would allow the sale of petroleum products such as kerosene, gasoline and fuel oil that are refined in Japan on behalf of foreign oil companies on a consignment basis.
At present, there is a 50 percent limit on the sale of such products unofficially set by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
The ministry is liberalising such sales as part of deregulatory steps it has been implementing since last year, the newspaper said.
Japanese oil refiners are consigned oil from companies mainly in China, South Korea, Taiwan and Singapore.
The output of such petroleum products accounts for an average of 5 percent to 6 percent of the nation's total processing of crude oil, which stands at 5 million barrels per day, the paper said.
